newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee steady vs dlr, SBI passive buyer.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee steady vs dlr, SBI passive buyer.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended nearly unchanged at 35.8175/8225 against the dollar on Thursday even as volumes on the inter-bank forex market fell, dealers said.
The State Bank of India (SBI) was a passive dollar buyer on Thursday as the bank had already covered most of its requirements ahead of a proposed nationwide strike on Thursday, dealers said.
The strike was called off early on Thursday.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) checked prices with some leading banks but did not appear to have intervened, dealers said.
"The rupee was rock steady today," said a dealer.
Inflows continued from foreign direct as well as portfolio investment, dealers said. Inflows from non-resident Indians continue unabated, officials at state-run banks said.
Forward premiums continued to fall on continued exporter sales and lack of buyers, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 4.07 percent compared to the previous close of 4.13 percent.
"There are no payers (of premium to buy forward dollars) in the market," a dealer at a Bombay bank said.
